plan.english: Mother, where is my father? He perished in the water at the ford. Why did he not get across? The current was strong, and it carried him off. Did you find his body? We did not find it. title: What we do for the dead

I will groan with you.

title: For a wife dead in childbirth

plan.english: Wife, you bore a daughter and you died. Your daughter groans in the darkness. She seeks your breast; she does not find it. Your loom is silent. The hearth in your dwelling is cold. I call your name; you do not hear. Mother Earth, guard her!

clauses.english: Wife, you bore a daughter and you died.
Your daughter groans in the darkness.
She seeks your breast; she does not find it.
Your loom is silent.
The hearth in your dwelling is cold.
I call your name; you do not hear.
Mother Earth, guard her!

plan.english: Brother, you lie in the field of the enemies. Dogs tear you; birds eat your eyes. No one laid you in the earth. No one washed your body. Your fame is imperishable. Your white bones lie in the field. I will go in the darkness and cover you.

clauses.english: Brother, you lie in the field of the enemies.
Dogs tear you; birds eat your eyes.
No one laid you in the earth.
No one washed your body.
Your fame is imperishable.
Your white bones lie in the field.
I will go in the darkness and cover you.

plan.english: House of my father, the fire devoured you. Your roof fell in the night. The fire burned the old man and my brothers. The smoke went up to the sky. I alone escaped. Now I sit in the ashes and shed tears.

clauses.english: House of my father, the fire devoured you.

plan.english: Wail, women, wail for the dead man! He lies on the wood; the fire devours him. His mother strikes her own breast. His widow tears her own cheeks. The smoke goes to Father Sky. May the gods receive him!

clauses.english: Wail, women, wail for the dead man!
He lies on the wood; the fire devours him.
His mother strikes her own breast.
His widow tears her own cheeks.
The smoke goes to Father Sky.
May the gods receive him!

plan.english: Mother Earth, we give you this mortal. Cover him with your hands. Do not give him to the dogs. Guard him from the wolves. May he rest in you. We set a stone; may his name not be lost.

clauses.english: Mother Earth, we give you this mortal.
Cover him with your hands.

plan.english: Perkʷunos, hear us! We give you this white bull. Drink his blood; eat his fat. Take the bull; do not take our young ones. Do not burn our houses. Strike the oaks and the stones!

clauses.english: Perkʷunos, hear us!
We give you this white bull.
Drink his blood; eat his fat.
Take the bull; do not take our young ones.
Do not burn our houses.

plan.english: Dead one, go away from our house! Do not come to our door at night. Lie under the stone; sleep in the darkness. We give you milk and meat. Eat and go! Fire, guard the door! Dogs, drive him away!

clauses.english: Dead one, go away from our house!

plan.english: There were two brothers, twins. There was no sky, and there was no sun. Then the one killed the other. From his flesh he made the earth. From his bones he made the stones. From his skull he made the sky. From his blood he made the waters. That was the first sacrifice. Now mortals kill bulls for the gods.

clauses.english: There were two brothers, twins.
There was no sky, and there was no sun.
Then the one killed the other.
From his flesh he made the earth.
From his bones he made the stones.
From his skull he made the sky.
From his blood he made the waters.
That was the first sacrifice.
Now mortals kill bulls for the gods.

plan.english: The king's ships lay there, and the wind did not come. The king asked the gods. The gods wanted his daughter. Then he led his own daughter to the altar. She wept, but he did not listen. He killed her with the knife. Then the wind arrived, and the ships went. The daughter did not return home. Her mother hates the king.

clauses.english: The king's ships lay there, and the wind did not come.
The king asked the gods.
The gods wanted his daughter.
Then he led his own daughter to the altar.
She wept, but he did not listen.
He killed her with the knife.
Then the wind arrived, and the ships went.
The daughter did not return home.
Her mother hates the king.

plan.english: Under the ford lives the water god. In summer he takes one man. He pulls him down by the feet. No one sees him. A young man did not tremble before the god. He went into the ford at night with his horse. In the morning the horse arrived home alone. The god took the young man and did not let him go. His mother searched for him at the ford for a year.

clauses.english: Under the ford lives the water god.
In summer he takes one man.
He pulls him down by the feet.
No one sees him.
A young man did not tremble before the god.
He went into the ford at night with his horse.
In the morning the horse arrived home alone.
The god took the young man and did not let him go.
His mother searched for him at the ford for a year.

plan.english: The path of the dead is long and dark. Two black dogs guard it. They let the good man go. They tear the lying man. Those whom no one laid in the earth do not reach the path. They walk among the houses in the darkness. So mortals lay the dead under stones.

clauses.english: The path of the dead is long and dark.
Two black dogs guard it.
They let the good man go.
They tear the lying man.
Those whom no one laid in the earth do not reach the path.
They walk among the houses in the darkness.
So mortals lay the dead under stones.

plan.english: The Allotter gives mortals their days. To one he gives many days, to another few. No one knows his own days. When the days are full, the Allotter comes. He seizes the child from its mother's breast, and he seizes the old man from the hearth. Gifts do not move him. Tears do not move him.

clauses.english: The Allotter gives mortals their days.
To one he gives many days, to another few.
No one knows his own days.
When the days are full, the Allotter comes.
He seizes the child from its mother's breast, and he seizes the old man from the hearth.
Gifts do not move him.
Tears do not move him.

plan.english: A serpent was lying at the ford. It drank the water, and the river dried up. It devoured the children of the village. The mothers groaned, and the gods were silent. Then Perkʷunos came, and he slew the serpent. He split its belly, and the waters came out. But the children did not return home.

plan.english: A herdsman was driving the cows to the stream. The snow was melting, and the stream was big. At the ford a cow slipped. The herdsman went into the water. The current seized him, and he sank. The cow swam out; the man did not come up. In the evening his wife found him on the stones. She sat down by him and shed tears. The village sang for him for three days.

plan.english: In winter the wolves arrived at the village. A boy was guarding the sheep at the fence. A she-wolf climbed over the fence. She seized the boy and pulled him away. The dogs ran, but she fled into the trees. The men followed her in the snow. They found only blood. His mother tore her cheeks in the snow.

plan.english: A young bride was carrying a child in the womb. When the birth came, the women gathered in the house. In the night she suffered pain, and she called on the gods. At dawn a son was born. Then her blood poured out, and she died. They laid her by the hearth. Her husband lifted him and set a name on him. The boy lived and grew up.

title: The burning of the chief's house

plan.english: Enemies came in the darkness to the chief's house. They piled wood around the house. They shut the door, and they threw fire on the wood. Inside the chief and his kin were sleeping. The roof fell in the fire. No one came forth. Only a daughter fled through the smoke. She told it in the village, and the men groaned.

plan.english: The king left the dead man in the field for the dogs. No one covered him; all trembled before the king. Then his sister came in the darkness. With her hands she threw earth on him. She poured out water and milk, and she chanted for him. The dogs did not eat him. In the morning the king caught sight of it, and he raged.

plan.english: Death took the chief in the autumn. His sons washed him and clothed him in white wool. They laid him on the wood. They killed his horse. Then the fire devoured the chief and the horse. The women wailed for nine days. They gathered his bones and hid them in a hole. They raised a stone; his fame is imperishable.
